blocks.value: Every program so far did one thing at a time. Concurrency lets a program do several, keep a user interface responsive while loading a file, handle many requests at once, use more than one CPU core.

It is also the hardest topic in this course, for a specific reason: **concurrent programs are not deterministic.** The same code with the same input can produce different results on different runs. Bugs appear once in a thousand executions and vanish when you look for them. Approach this lesson knowing that "it worked when I ran it" proves very little.
What you will be able to do
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

items: Define thread, process, concurrency, and context switch
Create threads by extending `Thread` and by implementing `Runnable`
Explain why thread output order is not guaranteed
Recognise a race condition and fix it with `synchronized`
